old: One small word once quietly split in two — one path flew, the other stayed grounded in mystery.
It names a speckle-breasted songbird, but also, oddly, a sore mouth.
Its ancestor is echoed in German Drossel and Latin turdus — same bird, different tongues.
clues: This songbird's name has a whole flock of European cousins, sharing an ancient root with German Drossel and Latin turdus, the scientific name for its family.
A brown woodland songbird with a boldly speckled breast, kin to the blackbird and American robin, prized for rich, repeated phrases far sweeter than a sparrow's chirp.
The same name also means a yeast infection that leaves white patches in the mouth or throat, a separate sense whose origin remains murky.
